title: What goes on the wire for ZCC trusted networks: the v1 webTrustedNetwork and v2 trusted-networks APIs
aliases: zcc v1 vs v2 trusted networks

prose.text: Trusted networks have two API families: the v1 verb-suffixed `webTrustedNetwork` endpoints, which the captured contract describes, and the RESTful v2 `trusted-networks` endpoints, which only the Go SDK and the Terraform provider use. Their record shapes differ.
{{list-envelope}} The contract describes the list response differently {{divergence:v1-list-shape}}.
{{v1-criteria-strings}} How the provider splits and trims them is [[zcc.terraform.trusted-network-backend:csv-trim]].

The v1 `conditionType` is a string in the contract and an integer in the Go SDK {{divergence:condition-type-wire-type}}. Which code means All is open in [[zcc.trusted-networks.object:condition-type-values]].
{{mutation-response}} {{error-code}} {{delete-missing-silent}} The Python create returns that acknowledgement as its result: [[zcc.sdk-python.return-shapes:add-result-has-no-id]].
The paged envelope and its walk are in [[zcc.api.v2-wire]].

{{contract-v1-only}} The Terraform provider chooses between the two by probing the v2 list: [[zcc.terraform.field-fidelity:v1-backend-serves-tenants-without-v2]]. Whether v2 replaces v1, and whether the two share state, is open {{gap:v1-v2-coexistence}}.

v1-criteria-strings.statement: In v1 each criterion of a trusted network (`dnsServers`, `dnsSearchDomains`, `hostnames`, `resolvedIpsForHostname`, `ssids`, `trustedDhcpServers`, `trustedGateways`, `trustedSubnets`, `trustedEgressIps`) is one comma-separated string, not a list: the contract and the Go SDK type them as strings, the Python SDK's examples pass values such as '10.11.12.13, 10.11.12.14' and '' for unused criteria, and the Terraform provider's v1 adapter splits and joins them on commas, noting that the v1 API returns values like "10.0.0.5, 10.0.0.6".

v2-restful.statement: The Go SDK's v2 trusted networks live at `/zcc/papi/public/v2/trusted-networks` and use RESTful verbs: POST to the collection to create, and GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on the collection path followed by the numeric ID (`%s/%d`).

v2-record-shape.statement: A v2 trusted network as the Go SDK models it has an integer `id`, a string `conditionType`, a `name`, and its criteria as string arrays (`dnsServerIps`, `trustedSubnetIps`, `trustedGatewayIps`, `trustedDhcpServersIps`, `trustedEgressIps`, `resolvedIpsForHostname`); the v1 type holds its criteria as single strings, four of them under other keys (`dnsServers`, `trustedSubnets`, `trustedGateways`, `trustedDhcpServers`).

v2-type-filter.statement: The Go SDK says the v2 list endpoint's `type` parameter scopes the keyword search to one field, one of `NAME`, `DNS_SERVERS`, `DNS_SEARCH_DOMAINS`, `HOST_NAME_IP`, `TRUSTED_SUBNETS`, `TRUSTED_GATEWAYS`, `TRUSTED_DHCP_SERVERS`, `TRUSTED_EGRESS_IPS` or `SSID`, and that the keyword is a substring match, so its name lookup still matches the whole name on the client, ignoring case (`strings.EqualFold`).

mutation-response.statement: The Go SDK documents that v1 create and edit return only a status such as {"success":"true","errorCode":"0"}, not the trusted network, so it resolves the record by name after create and by ID after update. Recorded responses from one test tenant agree that neither returns the record, but differ on the create: there the API answered `{"conditionType" : 0, "active" : false}`, while the edit answered `{"success" : "true", "errorCode" : "0"}`.

error-code.statement: The Go SDK treats a mutation as failed only when `errorCode` is non-empty and not "0".

delete-missing-silent.statement: Deleting a v1 trusted network ID that does not exist returned HTTP 200 with `{"success" : "false", "errorCode" : "3005"}` in a recorded response, and the Go `DeleteTrustedNetwork` passes no response target and returns success whenever the request itself did not fail, so such a failure is silent in Go.

v1-list-shape.summary: The shape of the v1 trusted-network list response: the contract defines a bare array of records, while both SDKs read an object with `trustedNetworkContracts`.

positions.says: The contract's 200 response for `webTrustedNetwork/listByCompany` is an array of `TrustedNetworkContract` items.
The Go SDK decodes the list into an object with `totalCount` and `trustedNetworkContracts`.
The Python SDK takes the records from the response's `trustedNetworkContracts` key, defaulting to an empty list.
A recorded `listByCompany` response from one test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) is an object with `totalCount` and `trustedNetworkContracts`, as the SDKs expect.

v1-list-shape.impact: The recording supports the SDKs: a client built from the contract that expects an array fails on the object the API returned. If a tenant did send the bare array the contract describes, both SDKs would return an error, not an empty list: Go fails to decode an array into its response object, and Python's lookup on a list raises inside a block that returns the exception as the error.

condition-type-wire-type.summary: The wire type of the trusted network's `conditionType`: the Go SDK sends an integer, the API contract types it as a string of format byte, and the Python SDK's docstring documents a string.

positions.says: str (docstring only; the code passes the value through)
A recorded `listByCompany` response from one test tenant (recorded with SDK 1.9.13, Python SDK cassette) returns `conditionType` as a JSON number.

condition-type-wire-type.impact: A caller following the Python docstring or the contract may send "0" where the Go SDK sends 0; the recorded read returns a number, but whether the API accepts a string on write is not documented. The Terraform provider documents both string forms as accepted for its own input, which says nothing about the API.

v1-v2-coexistence.title: Whether the v2 trusted-network API replaces v1 and shares its records
v1-v2-coexistence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the v2 families (notification templates, ZIA posture profiles, trusted networks) coexist with the v1 endpoints, which are still present, and no source says whether v2 supersedes v1 or when a tenant should move. A v2 fetch of notification templates and ZIA posture profiles returned HTTP 404 on one tested gateway, which shows only that those routes were unavailable there.
v1-v2-coexistence.blocks: deciding whether a v1 and a v2 trusted network with the same name are the same object, and which family to automate against
